title: Family Name
paragraphs: I think it was a really good song that left a lasting impression. Father clapped—clap, clap, clap—and then Panda and Éclair followed suit. The mammoths, on the other hand, just seemed a bit bored and only clapped half-heartedly a few times.
“Wow, Elmero and Kou, that was really great. It’s… the kind of singing that really touches your heart, isn’t it?”
Father is praising Zou and Kou. I suppose so, I suppose so.
“What do you think? She seems quite talented, doesn’t she? In many ways, she’s been helping us alongside the Guardian Knight, Larsazusa.”

Father says this to the old mammoth, who’s representing the mammoths. The old mammoth is trying to look like he’s smiling, but to me, it seems like he’s just giving a wry smile in response to Father’s words.
“Well now, it’s quite embarrassing, really. For someone like Elmero to be selected as a Guardian Knight is an honor far beyond what I deserve. I’m delighted that the Shield Hero is pleased by this.”
Father offers a slightly ambiguous nod of agreement.

“But what about other matters? He’s always been—how shall I put it?—a clumsy, ill-mannered, and gloomy child. I’m constantly anxious about whether he’s truly fit to protect the Shield Hero, bring him joy, and support him at the same time.”

Hmm… I don’t know much about his combat abilities, but isn’t he fighting effectively in coordination with Panda and Éclair? After all, according to Panda, he’s one of the top five warriors in Siltvelt. Despite that, his phrasing—as if he’s completely inadequate—bothers me a bit.

“From the perspective of the Phant family, Elmero is nothing more than a greenhorn who just happened to capture a relative of the traitor Takt… We’d really like to select someone more suitable to replace her. I believe replacing him with this child’s older sister or Lumes—who introduced us to the garden—would allow us to better fulfill our duty of guarding His Lordship the Shield Hero.”
“It seems he’s been neglecting his training to protect His Lordship the Shield Hero while indulging in singing…”

The Kebamammoths chuckle derisively at Zou. Zou hangs his head, and Kou looks indignant. Just as Kou tries to take a step forward, Zou blocks him and, with a slightly sad smile, seems to be admonishing him. To embarrass Kou like that… It seems these fellows are asking for trouble.
“I’m not so sure about that… At the very least, judging from his guard duty at the castle, as well as his training and practice, his skills seem to me to be second to none…”
“No, no. As far as I’m concerned, he’s still just a greenhorn. As a member of the Puhant family, this child’s lack of that wild, manly ferocity has long been a source of concern for our clan.”

“Wild, manly, and fierce… hmm. I hear Elmero is quite a famous fighter in Zeltoble. I hear he’s so popular he even has a nickname… and that those close to him were said to have lamented that he couldn’t return to Zeltoble because he’d become my Guardian Knight.”
This is… Father is asking the Mammoth family, as if strangling them with cotton, what exactly there is to mock about an elephant. The battle has already begun, hasn’t it! That’s Father for you.
“The members of my household are each worth a thousand men. Just because he’s gained popularity in a lowly country like Zeltoble doesn’t mean he’s anyone we need to worry about.”
“Well, all the nobles of Siltvelt say things like that, don’t they?”

Panda shows a certain degree of agreement here. With Panda on their side, the Mammoth family seems to be getting a little carried away by his opinion… but this is a trap. At this point, the old Mammoth strokes his tusk and shoots a contemptuous glance at the Elephant. Come to think of it… this old Mammoth has one tusk that’s broken off partway.

“O Shield Hero… How about making me your Guardian Knight instead of Elmero? I can do everything much better than Elmero—my grades, my combat skills… and even when it comes to nighttime matters… as a woman, too.”

No, even Father wouldn’t stand a chance against that flashy mammoth. Just how wide do you think Father’s “strike zone” is? I did recommend an elephant to him as a good match, but I was only hoping for a “like” kind of relationship.
…No, Father is the kind of person who can get along well with Big Sister and even a panda. Perhaps what matters is mentality, not appearance. He truly values the heart, doesn’t he?
Hm? I feel like Big Sister from the first world is saying something. It must just be my imagination. It’s just that Father’s “out zone” includes younger women.
“…So you’re saying you surpass everything about Elmero-san?”
“Yes, after all, that girl… is a bit clumsy.”
“Is that… what you think, too?”

Father even asks the Old Mammoth. Based on his words alone, it looks like he’s angry, but he’s just pretending not to know—as if to say, “Really? Is that so?” Father’s acting is terrifying, isn’t it? If people didn’t know better, they’d all be on the edge of their seats.
“Yes.”
“Whoa… that’s amazing. Just as you’d expect from a country like Siltvelt. I haven’t been here long, but this place really has… a lot of depth, doesn’t it?”
Seeing Father feign interest, the Mammoth family looks thoroughly pleased. I’m sure he’s referring to the depth of their foolishness.
“So, from this family’s perspective, Elmero isn’t worth considering, is he?”

“Of course, there are plenty of people far more capable than this child. As for the important role of Guardian Knight—a position fraught with anxiety—I’d much rather entrust it to someone else than Elmero. After all, he’s my unworthy grandson, so even letting him bear our family name is…”
He’s trying to appear humble, but it’s obvious at a glance that he’s actually looking down on her from the bottom of his heart.
“…You’re certainly right.”

Father has begun to exude an aura that sends a chill down the spine—one that only those close to him would recognize. Starting with Yuki-chan, Éclair and Panda sense that aura, and their expressions grow tense.
“She’s not a good fit for this family, is she?”
“…The Shield Hero?”
Oh? It seems Zou has noticed—that Father isn’t just going along with the insults directed at Zou.
“Yes!”

With Father’s agreement, the entire mammoth family—led by the old mammoth—nods in unison, gazing at Zou with contemptuous eyes and half-smiles. As for Zou, I’m a little annoyed with him, too. Kou looks like he’s about to pounce now that his beloved Zou is being mocked… just like the look on Keel’s face when I tore into that crepe.
“Please, Shield Hero, do say it. That Elmero isn’t a good fit for our family.”

Convinced that their seduction had been a complete success, the Old Mammoth and the Flashy Mammoth—certain of victory—start egging Zou on to get rid of Father. You see, It’s clear they think that if Father gives his endorsement, they can have the Guardian Knight dismissed and make the Spiky Mammoth his aide. They’re incredibly simple-minded, aren’t they?
“That’s right.”
Father stands up and walks over to Zou.
“As the Shield Hero, I command you: Strip Guardian Knight Elmero-Puhant of the Puhant family name.”
Zou looks at Father with an expression of disbelief, as if he’s seen something terrifying.
“Iwatani~…”
Kou glares at Father with all his might. Yet, his expression is truly manly.
“…Do you have a problem with that? It’s the truth, isn’t it?”
But Father… glared back at Kou with the same piercing gaze he had in the first world.
“Ah, wa-wa… I… I won’t lose. Uuuuugh~…”
Kou shows a slight flicker of fear at Father’s intense expression, but he quickly regains his composure and assumes a stance ready to pounce at any moment.
“Hahaha… I must say, the Shield Hero’s opinion is absolutely correct. Elmero, you may leave for wherever you please. You will never be allowed to cross the threshold of this house again.”

The old mammoth, now completely carried away, drove the elephant even further away. Hmm? I think I heard a slight noise and the footsteps of a rat-beastman coming from the next room. He must have come to check on the situation.

“This conversation isn’t over yet… Elmero, from now on, you shall bear the Janon family name. I’ll arrange for a fiefdom for you later. I expect you to continue approaching matters with that diligent attitude. If you have any objections, I’ll hear them later. Well then… let’s head back to the castle with this important item. Make sure you bring it back safely.”
As if glancing back quickly, Father makes to leave the dining hall. It’s settled, then. It’s a bit different from what I’d anticipated, but it’s quite a refreshing turn of events.
“Y-yes!”
Zou, who had been staring blankly, snapped back to his senses. Hearing Father’s words, he nodded and his expression brightened.
“What an elegant way to handle it. I don’t think Yuki would mind this kind of exchange.”
Yuki-chan, having grasped the situation, replied as she brushed her hair back.
“Hmm…?”

Kou couldn’t make sense of this turn of events and kept glancing back and forth between Zou and Father. As I stood up, Panda and Éclair also got to their feet, as if they were all getting ready to head home.
“What’s going on here?”
Kou asked Zou, looking completely confused.
“The Shield Hero isn’t trying to do anything terrible to me—he just said he wanted to reward me for my hard work.”
“Really? It kind of looked like Iwatani was trying to bully Elmero, but then it suddenly felt like things had changed—”
“That’s for sure. It might’ve been a bit too early for Kou to understand this.”
“Kou isn’t a kid!”
Just as we were about to leave, something like that happened.
“W-wait a minute!!”
At that moment, the old mammoth let out a voice resembling an angry shout directed at Father.
“What on earth is going on here?!”
“…There’s nothing to ‘what’s going on’ about it. Did you even know under what pretext I came to this house?”
Father turned slightly to face the Mammoth family, his gaze reminiscent of his counterpart from the first world, and replied.

“I came to greet his family because I held Knight Elmero’s professional conduct in high regard. Despite that, just think back on what his family did. Whether openly or behind my back, they did nothing but mock me—saying things like I wouldn’t be able to protect Knight Elmero if anything happened… and to top it off, they made this strange claim that there was someone else more suitable.”

Father says this with a very deep sigh. How should I put it… I can only say that, for such simple-minded people, they were weaving a web of foolish schemes. They come across as foolish people who pretend to be intellectuals even though they lack intelligence. They’re probably a race that rose to power through military exploits rather than wisdom.

“If they’d simply introduced someone from their own family, I suppose I could have put up with it. But it’s no fun having someone I hold in high regard ridiculed. You lot… don’t you realize just how terribly mistaken you are?”
Father declared this to the old mammoth with a look of contempt.

“If you let him keep talking, he’ll become even more brazen… Not content with merely defending that disgrace to the family, he’s boasting about his status as a new noble, his family name—and to top it off, he’s a Janon! To hear that intellectual little runt’s family name mentioned here—this is nothing short of a farce!”
“…Is that what you really think? How appalling. In that case, aren’t you much the same as Melromarc?”

That’s right. I know because I’ve been through this loop countless times. Fundamentally, there isn’t much difference between Melromarc and Siltvelt besides their race. At most, Siltvelt is a bit more manly for racial reasons. By the way, Melromarc is institutionally effeminate.
“Who do you think you are, acting like that as a mere human! Even if you’re the Shield Hero, I won’t forgive you!”
“So what if I’m human? If you’re this enraged at a human, doesn’t that mean you lot are even lower than that?”
Father is acting just like he did in the first world. My shivers are starting to turn into butterflies in my stomach.
“Don’t you realize that if you weren’t in the position of the Shield Hero, you’d be nothing but a slave in the Siltvelt!”

“I was sick and tired of sensing that condescending true intent here and there—no, in every single one of your glances. It’s painfully obvious you’re trying to use my position to climb the social ladder. And on top of that, you make fun of Elmero. You’re hopeless. Honestly… I can’t help but feel sorry for Elmero.”
With a “Oh, come on” sort of expression, Father shakes his head and speaks in a lecturing tone.

“What if I weren’t the Shield Hero? What are you talking about? I’m standing before you as the Shield Hero, so I have no obligation to entertain your ‘what-ifs.’ If I were to say that, what would it matter if you weren’t nobles? Think about it carefully.”
“You—”

The old mammoth looks so furious that steam seems ready to pour out of his head. Well, judging by his appearance, he seems to be more of a brute than a brainiac. He’s probably at a loss for words when facing Father. In that sense, wouldn’t the elephant be better at this kind of exchange? After all, it seems he managed to hold his own quite well as a mercenary, separate from the panda.

The old mammoth looks like he’s about to pounce on Father at any moment. The other mammoths, who had been standing around flustered, sense that the situation is escalating and start moving to try and stop him.
